plan.title: bug(ci): Blacksmith failover skips while required jobs are still unclaimed — merge-gate has no GH-hosted twin (#2672/#3168 residual)

narratives.Description: Unclaimed means no runner_name (not started_at, not reusable-workflow caller in_progress). capacity-arm must not skip while TS primary, Go primary, or merge-gate is unclaimed. Add GH-hosted merge-gate twin + required aggregator. Same-run rerun must re-evaluate the arm. Never cancel a claimed runner (#2652). Do not implement on PR #3333. Cite #3340. Refs #2672 #3168 #3333.
narratives.Overview:
## TL;DR

#2672 / #3168 give TypeScript and Go a Blacksmith primary plus a timed GH-hosted failover. That path can decide **skip** while a required Blacksmith job is still **unclaimed**, then never convert it. **Merge gate** (`task check`) has **no** GH-hosted twin at all. On a known us-west outage (2026-08-13), PR #3333 sat with merge-gate and TS primary queued, no `runner_name`, failovers already skipped. A claimed-but-dead runner is already forbidden to cancel (#2652). An **unclaimed sit after skip** is the missing recovery.

This is not a babysit-weather issue. #3167 / #3180 only tell the agent to wait. They do not make the required check finish.

## Evidence (PR #3333, SHA `56b8ae4997009ab4e885468053f655f85f7a1a1f`)

Blacksmith incident: [Partial outage in us-west](https://status.blacksmith.sh/cmsrg61yg09vd0lo9s1eagibm) — Identified / major. Upstream us-west cooling-power / thermal event. Latest update (15:11 UTC 2026-08-13): no ETA. They also pointed at GitHub [webhooks incident](https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/k8vbzwqjkxzn).

**First CI run** (`31711793724` first attempt):

- TypeScript (Blacksmith primary): success
- Merge gate (task check): success on Blacksmith
- Go (Blacksmith primary): **queued**, no runner
- Go / TS GH-hosted failover: **skipped**
- Capacity arm: success, failover skipped
- Go aggregator (`Go (test + build)`): in progress, polling the primary (up to 6h when `WANT_FAILOVER=false`)

So the first sit was **Go still queued after failover had already skipped**. Merge-gate failover would not have helped that attempt.

**After cancel + `rerun` of the same run id:**

- Same run `31711793724` came back `queued` (no new run id)
- Capacity arm finished in ~10s with “primaries claimed or done”
- Both GH-hosted failovers **skipped again**
- Go primary then **claimed** `blacksmith-01kzxpxsde27pr2ccqkzjrqz1e-4vcpu` and finished **success** in ~98s (15:22:53–15:24:31Z) — claimed + step timestamps moving = actually active
- Merge gate and TypeScript primary stayed **queued** with **no `runner_name`** but a `started_at` already set
- `POST .../actions/jobs/{id}/cancel` from the operator PAT returned **404**; in-workflow `cancel-queued-ci-primary.py` is the only cancel path, and it already ran

`cancel-queued-ci-primary.py` treats `started_at` or `runner_name` as claimed and will not cancel. Watchdog `pending` is only `queued` / `missing`. A reusable-workflow **caller** can look started / in_progress while the inner `/run` job is still waiting for a Blacksmith runner. The arm then exits skip. Nothing in that run will start failover later.

## Why #2672 / #3168 are not this issue

| Closed work | What it covers | What it does not |
|-------------|----------------|------------------|
| #2672 | TS/Go Blacksmith primary + timed GH-hosted failover | Merge-gate; claimed-vs-unclaimed detection |
| #3168 | Arm failover when the **watchdog is cancelled**; cancel unclaimed primaries before failover starts | Arm skip while a required job is still unclaimed; rerunning the same run keeps skip |
| #3167 / #3180 | `pr:watch` weather codes + status-page attribution | Making the required check finish |

Merge gate in `ci.yml` is `runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404` with no ubuntu-latest twin and no aggregator failover. Even a perfect TS/Go failover still leaves the required merge check waiting on us-west.

## What would have auto-proceeded (and what would not)

- **Merge-gate twin only:** would **not** have saved the first run (merge-gate was already green; Go was the sit). Would **not** have saved the rerun unless the arm also started that twin.
- **Arm must not skip while unclaimed (correct claim = `runner_name`):** would have failed over **Go** on the first run. TS + merge-gate were already green → required checks could go green → the #3273 closer could merge. That is the first-run automatic path.
- **Rerun + merge-gate twin + arm that still skips in 10s:** merge-gate failover never starts. Still a sit.
- **Full set below:** stall budget (~20 min) then failover. Automatic. Not instant. Not a 24h queue sit.

## Ask (thin, fail-closed — #3265)

1. **Unclaimed means no `runner_name`.** Do not treat `started_at` or reusable-workflow caller `in_progress` as a claimed runner. #2652 still forbids cancelling a job that has a runner name.
2. **`capacity-arm` / watchdog must not skip** while any required Blacksmith job (TS primary, Go primary, **merge-gate**) is unclaimed. Stall budget then cancel-unclaimed + arm failover, same as #3168 intended for the lanes.
3. **Merge-gate gets a GH-hosted twin** and a required aggregator so a cancelled/unclaimed Blacksmith merge-gate can still go green (same shape as TS/Go aggregators).
4. **Same-run rerun must re-evaluate the arm.** A cancelled run that is `rerun` must not keep the old skip while jobs are still unclaimed.

Out of scope: `--skip-ci` as the recovery; cancelling a claimed runner (#2652); rewriting Greptile floors; babysit-only weather text; fixing this on PR #3333.

## Acceptance sketch

- A fixture / test of `classify-ci-job-state` + `cancel-queued-ci-primary`: job `status=queued` or `in_progress` with `started_at` set and **no** `runner_name` is **unclaimed** (cancelable / failover-armable). A job with `runner_name` is claimed (do not cancel).
- A reusable-workflow caller that is `in_progress` without a Blacksmith `runner_name` on the inner suite job does not make the arm skip that suite.
- Merge-gate unclaimed past the stall budget arms a GH-hosted merge-gate; the required merge-gate aggregator can go green when that twin succeeds, even if the Blacksmith merge-gate was cancelled unclaimed.
- After GitHub reruns a cancelled CI run, if a required Blacksmith job is still unclaimed, failover is armed (not left skipped from the prior attempt).
- Existing claimed-runner rule unchanged: never cancel `in_progress` with a runner name.
- CHANGELOG cites this issue. Refs #2672 #3168 #2652 #3333.

## Related

- Residual of #2672 (lane failover) and #3168 (arm when watchdog cancelled)
- Observed on PR #3333 during Blacksmith us-west outage 2026-08-13
- #3167 / #3180 remain the agent weather surface; this issue is the **workflow** recovery
- Do not expand PR #3333 to implement this (#2881)
